hyps.why: A conv on edge 0 makes node 1 informative, so a conv on edge 4 adds a real deeper path.
With a conv already on the direct 0-3 edge, an extra conv into node 3 has diminishing returns.
Replacing a skip that already carries signal gains less than replacing none, which opens a dead path.
The direct 0-3 skip is already a strong residual path, so converting it to conv adds less than filling an empty edge.
Replacing none with conv restores a missing path into node 2, a bigger gain than swapping one existing op for another.
With edge 0 removed node 1 is dead, so a conv on edge 4 has almost nothing to process.
Filling the empty direct input-output edge with a conv gives a much larger gain than upgrading an existing op.
A conv alternative path into node 3 compensates for the removed direct edge, shrinking the loss.
Removing a conv on the direct edge loses far more than removing a pool, 1x1 or an already-absent edge.
With edge 4 already absent, removing edge 5 cuts the node 1/2 route into the output and leaves only the direct edge 3.
